stem: Which of the following best describes the clinical definition of a birthmark?

options.text: A skin lesion that must be present exactly at birth
An imbalance or preponderance of specific skin components, such as melanocytes or blood vessels
A temporary skin discoloration caused exclusively by birth trauma
A growth consisting solely of overactive sweat glands and nerve fibres
A benign skin infection that develops in early infancy

explanation: Birthmarks are an imbalance or preponderance of normal skin components such as pigment cells or blood vessels.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because birthmarks may not be obvious at the moment of birth and can become apparent later.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because birthmarks are described as an imbalance or preponderance of specific skin components, such as melanocytes or blood vessels.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because birthmarks are structural skin changes, not temporary discolouration caused only by birth trauma.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because birthmarks are not defined as lesions composed solely of sweat glands and nerve fibres.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because birthmarks are not skin infections; they are developmental changes in skin components.

source.hint: Consider the structural composition of the skin and when these lesions typically appear.
